note: Adjudicated accidental variants (punctuation only). Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero divergence — the Mass wording is letter for letter the wording the corpus already carries as the prayer on its own (orationes.pater-noster).

adjudicated.ruling: Full stop after Orémus, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.aufer-a-nobis w001. The invitation to pray is a complete utterance; DO's colon is a consequence of its layout, which runs the preface onto the same line.

Comma after formáti, with handmissal-eo. Two parallel participial phrases stand before the main verb — móniti by the precepts, formáti by the institution — and DO sets the comma after the first but not after the second, which is inconsistent within its own line.

Full stop, with do. The petitions are separate sentences, as the corpus already sets them at orationes.pater-noster; handmissal-eo's colons are that edition's way of keeping the prayer visually continuous. The same ruling governs w019, w022 and w037.
No comma before et, with do. In cælo et in terra is a single pair governed by sicut and is not divided.
Full stop, with do and with every other Amen in this corpus; handmissal-eo leaves this one unpointed alone among its own Amens on the same page.
